primary_cause: Ad-market estimates deteriorated sharply Mar 27 with Cowen projecting Google Facebook Twitter Snap would lose more than $40B of 2020 ad revenue. U.S. initial jobless claims exploded to 3.28M on Mar 26. Investors repriced Google ad exposure as small-business advertisers shut down
secondary_factors: Profit-taking after three-day stimulus rally. General megacap-tech derisking
store_description: Google key vulnerability was not search usage but advertising monetization. With analysts suddenly quantifying a massive pandemic-driven ad hit and jobless claims coming in far worse than even already-bad expectations the market likely treated GOOG as an ad cyclical rather than a pure defensive tech name.

primary_cause: No new Apple-specific negative Mar 24-27. Live issue remained COVID-driven demand and supply disruption across consumer electronics. Apple already warned earlier coronavirus would hurt production and China sales. Reversal in cyclically exposed megacap tech
secondary_factors: Post-rally profit-taking. Broader recession fears after 3.28M jobless-claims shock
store_description: On March 27 Apple looked less like a safe haven and more like a global hardware and consumer-demand proxy. In the absence of fresh good news strong enough to offset recession fears the stock appears to have traded down on persistent worries about iPhone demand and supply-chain disruption.

primary_cause: Accenture had just reported results and market focused on reduced visibility into client spending as COVID spread. Stock falling despite beat as investors zeroed in on weaker near-term expectations. Fear enterprise consulting and outsourcing spend would slow materially
secondary_factors: Broad recession concerns after jobless-claims print
store_description: Accenture issue was not a bad quarter so much as clients freezing discretionary work. In a market suddenly pricing deep recession investors treated ACN consulting and digital-transformation pipeline as vulnerable to corporate budget cuts despite relatively resilient current results.

primary_cause: No clearly dated Mar 24-27 Adobe-specific negative headline. Adobe had posted strong quarterly results but investors reassessing whether marketing and creative software demand would soften. Valuation compression in software after stimulus bounce
secondary_factors: Macro risk-off after terrible labor data. Concern enterprise and SMB spending would weaken
store_description: Adobe had beaten numbers but that was not enough to protect a premium-multiple software name when the market shifted from backward-looking earnings to forward-looking recession risk. The likely read-through was slower seat expansion weaker SMB demand and softer marketing spend.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC. Broadcom had already withdrawn its 2020 revenue forecast because of coronavirus-related demand and supply disruption. Lingering fallout from withdrawn outlook and concern over handset and enterprise semiconductor demand
secondary_factors: General tech-cyclical selling into recession fears
store_description: Even though the forecast withdrawal came earlier in March it was still the key unresolved overhang by March 27. Investors were likely extrapolating weaker smartphone networking and enterprise demand as shutdowns spread globally.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC. American Express said Mar 17 spending volumes fell at end of February and into March. Later disclosure showed travel and entertainment about 30% of proprietary volumes in 2019 down almost 95%. Collapse in travel-and-entertainment card spend
secondary_factors: Record jobless claims. Widening consumer-credit concerns
store_description: AXP was one of the clearest COVID consumer-finance casualties because its business mix was unusually exposed to travel restaurants and corporate T&E. By March 27 investors were likely pricing not just lower billed business but also higher credit losses if layoffs accelerated.

primary_cause: Boeing publicly thanked Washington for passage of CARES Act Mar 26 but market wrestling with strings attached to federal support and brutal collapse in commercial aviation. Ongoing solvency and liquidity fears tied to airline shutdown and uncertainty around bailout terms
secondary_factors: 737 MAX overhang. Fear of equity dilution and debt-heavy rescue
store_description: Boeing drop was much more severe than the average industrial because investors still viewed it as a capital-structure story not just an earnings story. The CARES package may have helped the system but it also highlighted how dependent Boeing and its customers had become on emergency financing.

primary_cause: Big U.S. banks had already halted buybacks Mar 15. Mar 26 jobless-claims report showed 3.28M new claims. Rapidly worsening credit-loss expectations as unemployment exploded
secondary_factors: Zero-rate pressure on net interest margins. Recession fears
store_description: BAC traded like a macro credit proxy. The combination of record claims buyback suspension and the market fast-rising expectations for reserve builds made large consumer banks structurally vulnerable even without a new BAC-specific headline.

primary_cause: Booking had already withdrawn Q1 guidance due to worsening COVID impact on travel demand. Travel remained in free fall. Complete collapse in global travel bookings
secondary_factors: Balance-sheet and liquidity fears. Uncertainty about how long lockdowns would last
store_description: BKNG much larger-than-market decline fits a business whose revenue is almost directly tied to nights booked and air travel. By March 27 investors still had no visibility on when hotel airline and cross-border demand would normalize so the stock kept trading as one of the purest pandemic losers.

primary_cause: Reuters described coronavirus as the greatest test yet of bond-market liquidity. Concern around asset values flows and fee pressure during ETF and fixed-income market stress
secondary_factors: Broad financial-sector weakness after jobless-claims shock
store_description: BlackRock was less about credit losses than about market plumbing and AUM sensitivity. In late March 2020 any asset manager with huge ETF and fixed-income exposure was vulnerable to worries about outflows spread widening and fee-bearing asset declines.

primary_cause: Citi joined peers in suspending stock repurchases. Mar 26 claims report showed 3.28M new unemployed. Expected surge in loan losses and reserve builds in severe recession
secondary_factors: Lower rates hurting bank profitability
store_description: Citi international and consumer-credit exposure made it a straightforward recession trade on March 27. The market was no longer focusing on capital return it was focusing on how large the eventual credit bill would be.

primary_cause: No fresh AMAT-specific Mar 24-27 negative headline. Semiconductor complex remained under pressure from demand disruption tied to coronavirus. Cyclical semiconductor-capex fears as customers reconsidered spending
secondary_factors: Supply-chain risk. Broad tech-cyclical selling
store_description: Equipment names like AMAT often sell off harder than semis themselves when investors start pricing a capex freeze. By March 27 the likely interpretation was that memory foundry and logic customers would conserve cash until end-demand visibility improved.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC context. Comcast Universal theme parks said Mar 24 would remain closed through Apr 19. Olympic postponement put more than $1.25B of NBCUniversal ad commitments into limbo. Direct hit to parks plus disruption to NBC major advertising event
secondary_factors: Broader ad-market weakness. Recession fears
store_description: Comcast was being repriced as a hybrid of media theme parks and advertising rather than just broadband. The extension of park closures and the Tokyo Olympics delay both struck businesses investors had counted on for 2020 revenue support.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC context. GE had already warned coronavirus could hit Q1 cash flow by $300M-$500M mainly through aviation. Mar 24 GE highlighted ventilator ramp but far too small to offset aviation stress. Worsening aviation and liquidity fears
secondary_factors: Industrial recession risk. Leverage concerns
store_description: The market cared far more about collapsing airline demand and engine-service revenue than about GE Healthcare ventilator upside. GE traded down because investors viewed the company as highly exposed to the most damaged part of the industrial economy: commercial aerospace.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC. Caterpillar withdrew 2020 outlook Mar 26 and suspended some operations citing economic uncertainty weaker equipment demand and supply-chain disruption. Explicit withdrawal of guidance and plant shutdowns
secondary_factors: Fear of collapse in construction mining and oil-related capex
store_description: This was one of the clearest stock-specific catalysts. Once CAT pulled guidance and acknowledged operational suspensions the market had a direct signal that end-market demand and factory continuity were deteriorating faster than expected.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC. FedEx had just suspended FY2020 profit outlook Mar 18. Quarterly adjusted net income fell 53.5% YoY to $371M or $1.41/share on revenue of about $17.5B. Withdrawal of guidance and mounting concern global trade and TNT turnaround would worsen
secondary_factors: Recession fears despite parcel demand tailwinds
store_description: FedEx stock could not fully benefit from stay-at-home delivery winner logic because the market was staring at collapsing business activity and a very uncertain earnings path. The guidance suspension told investors management itself could not underwrite near-term visibility.

primary_cause: No new Reuters Disney-specific Mar 24-27 headline beyond still-unfolding shutdown backdrop. Disney remained hit across parks theatrical releases and sports. Investors continued to reprice Disney as one of largest multi-segment COVID losers
secondary_factors: Park closures. Frozen film slate. ESPN ad and sports disruption
store_description: Unlike many media names Disney had enormous offline exposure: parks cruises theaters and live sports. By March 27 the absence of near-term reopening visibility meant every one of those cash engines was being marked down at once.

primary_cause: STOCK-SPECIFIC. Chevron cut 2020 capex by 20% lowered Permian production guidance by 125,000 boe/d and suspended buybacks as oil demand cratered. Oil-price collapse and Chevron own capex and output reset
secondary_factors: Broader energy-sector liquidation tied to demand shock and Saudi-Russia price war backdrop
store_description: CVX drop reflects both macro oil panic and a very concrete company response. Once Chevron slashed spending by $4B and pulled back Permian ambitions investors had confirmation that even a supermajor was moving into defense mode.

primary_cause: No clearly dated Mar 24-27 Emerson-specific negative headline. Dragged by industrial and oil-exposed peers into recession repricing. Exposure to industrial automation and energy capex in suddenly frozen economy
secondary_factors: Sympathy move with CAT GE and oil-linked industrials after CAT withdrew guidance and Chevron cut spending
store_description: Emerson end markets made it vulnerable even without an obvious standalone headline. On March 27 investors were clearly punishing companies tied to factory spending process industries and energy capex as shutdowns spread globally.

primary_cause: No fresh negative Salesforce-specific corporate headline Mar 24-27. Mar 27 company messaging was largely about employee and community COVID response. Multiple compression and broad selling in enterprise software after relief rally
secondary_factors: Concern enterprise customers would delay new software projects despite remote-work demand tailwinds
store_description: CRM was probably hit less by a single news item than by the market sudden refusal to pay up for growth software during peak macro uncertainty. Investors likely worried that even mission-critical cloud vendors would see slower deal cycles as customers triaged budgets.
